newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields drift higher at close in sidelined mkt.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields drift higher at close in sidelined mkt.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.05 PCT (PREV 9.15) US 5-YR 5.85 (PREV 5.84)
* NZ bonds finish slightly weaker on thin flows
* Market waits for government, RBNZ's MPS
* Money market closes slightly weaker but still strong
New Zealand yields drifted higher in a sidelined market at Wednesday's close after what dealers said was a very ordinary day.

Flows were light other than some curve play, with outright interest holding back until the market saw either a resolution on the political front or some clues on monetary conditions from the Reserve Bank, in its December 17 monetary policy statement.

New Zealand is currently without a government after an inconclusive general election on October 12. The nationalist New Zealand First Party is negotiating separately with both the caretaker National Party government and the centre-left Labour Party over the shape of the new government.

Hopes that a coalition deal might be struck this week were fading, dealers said, but the market was holding tight to its hopes NZ First would swing National's way. Parliament is due to convene for the first time by December 13.
The mid bonds ended five points weaker, while the longer maturities were off four.

"New Zealand has just been off the boil a little bit. There was a bit of a flurry this morning, people thinking maybe the market was going to back up, but I can't see it doing anything until there are some reasonable flows," one dealer said.
"I get the impression those who are long are waiting for it to rally to sell into, and those who are short are waiting for it to pull back to buy. It's a fairly evenly matched market."
Ninety-day bank bills edged up a basis point to 8.39 percent while the front futures contract was down five points to 91.69.
Bill dealers said volumes were moderate, and although some weakness had been seen toward the close the money market was still looking strong.

"In the big scheme of things, four or five points is nothing much in the short end," one said. ---------------------------------------------------------------- Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD
